title: Flat integral finitely presented algebra which is an isomorphism modulo a radical ideal is an isomorphism
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$ (a Zariski pair). Let $A\to B$ be a ring map which is flat ($B$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]), integral (every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$) and of finite presentation ($B\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ as $A$-algebras for some $n,m\ge0$), and such that the induced map $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism. Then $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ELZ (lemma-check-isomorphism-zariski, line 2265) and its proof: A -> B finite (Algebra Lemma 02JJ lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral), B finitely presented as A-module (Algebra Lemma 0564 lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension), finite locally free (Algebra Lemma 00NX lemma-finite-projective), rank 1 along V(I) hence everywhere since every closed point lies in V(I), and a locally free algebra of rank 1 is an isomorphism ('pleasant exercise'); Definition Tag 0ELY (definition-zariski-pair)

proof.text: The finite-presentation hypothesis makes B a finite-type A-algebra. Since A -> B is integral, the integral-plus-finite-type criterion gives that B is a finitely generated A-module, so the ring map is finite.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ELZ, first sentence, citing Algebra Lemmas 02JJ and 0564

proof.text: By step 1, B is a finite A-module, and the finite-presentation hypothesis on the A-algebra B makes it a finitely presented A-module. With flatness, B is finite locally free. The quotient isomorphism A/I -> B/IB identifies every fibre over a prime containing I with a one-dimensional residue-field algebra. The rank-one propagation lemma therefore gives rankAtStalk B = 1 at every prime: the rank is locally constant, and if the locus where it differs from one were nonempty and closed, it would contain a maximal ideal; every maximal ideal contains I because I is in the Jacobson radical, contradicting the rank-one fibre calculation on V(I).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ELZ, middle argument: finite locally free, rank one on V(I), then rank one everywhere for a Zariski pair

proof.text: Apply the rank-one algebra-map criterion to the finite flat A-module B. Since rankAtStalk B is constantly one, the structure map A -> B is bijective, hence an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ELZ, final sentence: a locally free algebra of rank one is an isomorphism
